subject: Standardized LD measures for grm model

messages.author: 74a84137ff78cda0
messages.subject: Standardized LD measures for grm model
parts:
Phil,
I am new to this group so forgive any novice transgressions. I love mirt...

My question is - just what are the values that get reported when requesting LD measures for a grm model? Using the command 'residuals(mod1, type = 'LD')' gives me a set of X2 values below the diagonal and standardized values above the diagonal - correct? Since degrees of freedom is greater than 1 for a grm model and I cannot, therefore, use the 3.84 threshold value for the X2 values, how can I determine if a value is significant (although I may have seen in one of your posts that you are not necessarily interested in statistical significance). Moving along, I believe somewhere in your documentation you refer to the standardized values as correlations. If that is correct, can we interpret a standardized value as an 'effect size' and use Cohen's rules of thumb as a framework for interpretation. In another post, you mention .10 as a flag for possible concern which corresponds to a small effect size.

Am I mixing apples and oranges here?

Thanks for any help you can provide.

Jerry Bean
Ohio State University

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Standardized LD measures for grm model
parts: There's an option in the residuals function to save the degrees of freedom for each covariance pair, so if you really want to to a test for significance based on the X^2 distribution that would be how to go about it. The upper diagonal terms or just Cramer's V transformations to remove the effect of the df, and to get a more clear picture of dependence when cut-off values are supplied with suppress = #.
